questions.question: Taxus wallichiana Zucc (Himalayan yew) is a medicinal plant found in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The Himalayan Yew :

 
• The Himalayan Yew (Taxus wallachiana) is a medicinal plant found in various parts of Himachal Pradesh and Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• The plant holds an important place in traditional medicine and its products are used by the local populations for treating common infections. 
 
• A chemical compound called ‘taxol’ is extracted from the bark, needles, twigs and roots of this tree, and it has been successfully used to treat some cancers – the drug is now the biggest selling anti-cancer drug in the world. 
 
• The species is under great threat due to over-exploitation.
 
• In the last decade, thousands of yew trees have dried up in various parts of Himachal Pradesh and Arunachal Pradesh.

 
• Yew has undergone a recent, range-wide population decline of at least 50% as per IUCN. 
 
• Due to the illegal cutting of plant parts and other anthropogenic pressures, Himalayan yew is endangered, and threatened with extinction, in Himalaya.
 
• Throughout its range in the western Himalayas, it is declining in response to a range of threats.
 
• In Afghanistan, up to 50% of the forests where it occurs have been destroyed or heavily logged (UNEP 2003) over the last 30 years.
 
• In northwest India and western Nepal, exploitation associated with Taxol production has led to a national decline of up to 90% in Taxus populations throughout the country.
 
• Also, in other countries such as Pakistan, overexploitation for fuel, fodder, and medicinal use has led to a significant decline.
 
• The decline is continuing and while the causes are largely understood, in many areas they will not be reversible. On this basis, an assessment of Endangered is warranted.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?

options.text: Mitochondria: Power house of the cell

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nucleus: Lipid metabolism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The nucleus is the control center of the cell, storing the cell's DNA and coordinating cellular activities such as growth, metabolism, and reproduction.
 
• Lipid metabolism is primarily associated with the smooth endoplasmic reticulum and not the nucleus.
 
• The nucleus is responsible for the transcription of DNA to mRNA, which is then translated into proteins by ribosomes.
 
• The nucleus also contains the nucleolus, which is involved in ribosome synthesis and assembly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lysosomes:**

 
 
• Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles that contain enzymes to break down biomolecules.
 
• They are often referred to as the "suicidal bags" of the cell because they can digest cellular components when the cell is damaged.
 
• They play a key role in the degradation and recycling of cellular waste, cellular signaling, and energy metabolism.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria:**
 
 
• Mitochondria are known as the "powerhouses of the cell" because they generate most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• They are involved in other processes such as signaling, cellular differentiation, and cell death, as well as the control of the cell cycle and cell growth.
 
• Mitochondria have their own DNA and are thought to have originated from ancestral prokaryotes through endosymbiosis.
 
 
 
• **Ribosomes:**
 
 
• Ribosomes are the molecular machines responsible for protein synthesis.
 
• They translate messenger RNA (mRNA) into amino acid sequences to build proteins.
 
• Ribosomes can be found floating freely in the cytoplasm or bound to the endoplasmic reticulum, forming the rough ER.
 
• They are made up of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins and consist of two subunits, a large and a small one.

questions.question: Which of the following battles is considered the formal beginning of the British Raj in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Battle of Plassey**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Battle of Plassey was fought on **23 June 1757**, in the eastern part of India.
 
• This battle marked the **beginning of British colonial rule in India**.
 
• It was fought between the British East India Company and the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj ud-Daulah.
 
• The British victory in this battle was **largely due to the betrayal of Nawab's commander, Mir Jafar**, who sided with the British.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Carnatic War**

 
 
• The First Carnatic War (1746-1748) was fought between the British and the French in India.
 
• It was mainly a result of the War of Austrian Succession in Europe.
 
• The war ended with the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle in 1748, resulting in a status quo ante bellum.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Wandiwash**
 
 
• The Battle of Wandiwash was fought on 22 January 1760 between the British and the French.
 
• The British, under Sir Eyre Coote, decisively defeated the French forces.
 
• This battle marked the end of French colonial ambitions in India.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Buxar**
 
 
• The Battle of Buxar was fought on 22 October 1764 between the British East India Company and the combined forces of the Nawab of Bengal, Nawab of Awadh, and the Mughal Emperor.
 
• The British victory established their supremacy in the eastern parts of India.
 
• This battle was crucial for the British as it consolidated their power after the Battle of Plassey.

questions.question: Which of the following Indian states has the least number of operational airports as of 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mizoram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mizoram is a state in Northeast India, known for its scenic beauty and cultural heritage.
 
• As of 2022, Mizoram has only one operational airport, which is Lengpui Airport.
 
• Lengpui Airport is located near Aizawl, the capital city of Mizoram, and is the primary airport serving the state.
 
• Due to the state's hilly terrain and lower population density, the development of multiple airports has been limited.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Operational Airports in India:**

 
 
• India has a network of airports spread across its vast geography, including both international and domestic airports.
 
• The Airports Authority of India (AAI) is responsible for the development, maintenance, and management of civil aviation infrastructure in the country.
 
• As of 2022, some states like Maharashtra and Karnataka have multiple operational airports due to their larger land area and higher population density.
 
 
 
• **Lengpui Airport:**
 
 
• Lengpui Airport is the only operational airport in Mizoram and serves as the main gateway to the state.
 
• It is situated approximately 32 km from Aizawl, the state capital.
 
• The airport is equipped to handle both domestic flights and is known for its picturesque approach due to the surrounding hills.
 
• Lengpui Airport was inaugurated in 1998 and has since been a crucial part of Mizoram's connectivity.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Airport Development in Hilly Regions:**
 
 
• Constructing and maintaining airports in hilly terrains like Mizoram presents unique challenges, including difficult topography and limited flat land availability.
 
• High construction costs and environmental concerns also play significant roles in limiting the number of airports.
 
• However, such regions can benefit greatly from air connectivity in terms of tourism and economic development.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Air Connectivity:**
 
 
• Air connectivity is crucial for the socio-economic development of any region, providing faster and more efficient transportation options.
 
• It facilitates trade, tourism, and cultural exchange, contributing to the overall growth of the region.
 
• For states like Mizoram, with challenging road infrastructure, air connectivity becomes even more important.

questions.question: Who among the following, while praising the amending feature of the Indian Constitution said that 'This variety in the amending process is wise but is rarely found'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**K C Wheare**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• K C Wheare was a distinguished constitutional scholar known for his work on federalism and constitutional law.
 
• He praised the Indian Constitution's amending process for its variety and flexibility, which he considered wise and unique.
 
• Wheare emphasized that such variety in the amending process is rare among the world's constitutions.
 
• His observations highlight the robustness and adaptability of the Indian Constitution in accommodating changes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Granville Austin**

 
 
• Granville Austin was an American historian who studied the Indian Constitution extensively.
 
• He is known for his seminal work, "The Indian Constitution: Cornerstone of a Nation," which examines the making and functioning of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Austin's work is highly regarded for its in-depth analysis and insight into the Indian constitutional process.
 
 
 
• **Ivor Jennings**
 
 
• Sir Ivor Jennings was a British lawyer and academic who made significant contributions to the study of constitutional law.
 
• He was involved in the drafting of several constitutions in the Commonwealth countries, including India.
 
• Jennings emphasized the importance of conventions and practices in the functioning of a constitution.
 
 
 
• **HM Seervai**
 
 
• H.M. Seervai was a prominent Indian jurist and constitutional expert.
 
• He authored the influential book "Constitutional Law of India," which is a comprehensive commentary on the Indian Constitution.
 
• Seervai's work is widely cited in legal circles and has greatly contributed to the understanding of the Indian constitutional law.
 
 
 
• **Amending Process in the Indian Constitution**
 
 
• The Indian Constitution provides a detailed procedure for its amendment in Part XX, Article 368.
 
• The amending process is categorized into three types: simple majority, special majority, and special majority with ratification by states.
 
• This flexibility allows the Constitution to be both rigid and flexible, accommodating necessary changes while maintaining stability.
 
• Amendments require different levels of parliamentary support and, in some cases, ratification by state legislatures, ensuring a broad consensus.

questions.question: Tabla player, Ustad Zakir Hussain was awarded which of the following awards by the Government of India in 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Padma Vibhushan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ustad Zakir Hussain, a renowned tabla player, was awarded the Padma Vibhushan by the Government of India in 2023.
 
• The Padma Vibhushan is the second-highest civilian award in India, recognizing exceptional and distinguished service in any field including service rendered by Government servants.
 
• Ustad Zakir Hussain is globally acclaimed for his virtuosity and contributions to Indian classical music.
 
• He has previously been awarded the Padma Shri in 1988 and the Padma Bhushan in 2002.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Padma Awards:**

 
 
• The Padma Awards are one of the highest civilian honors of India announced annually on the eve of Republic Day.
 
• The awards are given in three categories: Padma Vibhushan (for exceptional and distinguished service), Padma Bhushan (distinguished service of a high order), and Padma Shri (distinguished service).
 
• The awards recognize achievements in all fields of activities or disciplines where an element of public service is involved.
 
• The Padma Awards were instituted in the year 1954 and are announced every year on Republic Day (26th January).
 
 
 
• **Ustad Zakir Hussain:**
 
 
• Ustad Zakir Hussain is an Indian tabla virtuoso, composer, percussionist, music producer, and film actor.
 
• He is the son of legendary tabla player Ustad Alla Rakha.
 
• He has been awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, the highest Indian recognition given to practicing artists.
 
• In addition to his work in Indian classical music, he has also collaborated with many international artists and has contributed to various genres of music.

questions.question: Gangubai Hangal and Prabha Atre were exponents of the ________ Gharana.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kirana**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gangubai Hangal and Prabha Atre** were exponents of the **Kirana Gharana.**

 
 
• The Kirana Gharana is known for its focus on perfect intonation and the intricate use of microtones (shrutis).
 
• Gangubai Hangal was an Indian classical singer of the khyal genre of Hindustani classical music.
 
• Prabha Atre is also a renowned Indian classical vocalist from the same Gharana, known for her innovative approach and contributions to classical music.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Gharanas**

 
 
• **Rampur Gharana** is known for its mix of Dhrupad and Khayal styles.
 
• **Jaipur Gharana** is recognized for its intricate and complex singing style.
 
• The **Mewati gharana** is a Hindustani classical music apprenticeship tribe that was founded in the late 19th century by brothers Ghagge Nazir Khan and Wahid Khan of Indore.
 
 
• Key Exponents - Pandit Jasraj, Ustad Rais Khan, Mohd Shafi etc.

questions.question: Which of the following famous Indian athletes won the Zurich Diamond League final 2022 in September 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neeraj Chopra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Neeraj Chopra** is an Indian track and field athlete who competes in the javelin throw.
 
• He created history by becoming the first Indian to win a gold medal in athletics at the **Olympic Games** when he won the men's javelin throw at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.
 
• On 8th September 2022, Neeraj Chopra became the first Indian to win the Zurich Diamond League final with a throw of 88.44 meters.
 
• He has consistently performed well in international competitions, bringing laurels to India in the field of athletics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• **Zurich Diamond League**

 
 
• The Diamond League is an annual series of elite track and field athletic competitions comprising fourteen of the best invitational athletics meetings.
 
• It was founded in 2010, and the Zurich meeting is one of the most prestigious events in this series.
 
• Athletes accumulate points at each Diamond League meet and the top performers in each event compete in the final, where the winner is crowned the Diamond League champion.
 
 
 
• **Javelin Throw**
 
 
• Javelin throw is a track and field event where the javelin, a spear about 2.5 meters in length, is thrown.
 
• The objective is to throw the javelin as far as possible; the athlete with the longest valid throw wins.
 
• It has been a part of the modern Olympic Games since its inception for men in 1908 and for women in 1932.
 
 
 
• **Neeraj Chopra's Career Highlights**
 
 
• Neeraj Chopra won the gold medal at the 2018 Commonwealth Games and the 2018 Asian Games, where he also set a new Indian national record.
 
• He made his mark internationally by becoming the World Junior Champion in 2016.
 
• He is also the first Indian to win a Diamond League title, which he achieved in August 2022 in Lausanne before winning the Zurich final.

questions.question: Which of the following Table Tennis World Championship events was held in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**19th World Championships, 1952**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 19th World Table Tennis Championships were held in Bombay (now Mumbai), India, in 1952.
 
• This event marked the first time that the World Table Tennis Championships were hosted in India.
 
• The Championships featured both men's and women's events, including singles, doubles, and mixed doubles competitions.
 
• India's hosting of the event was significant in promoting the sport within the country and the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Table Tennis World Championships:**

 
 
• The Table Tennis World Championships are an international event organized by the International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF).
 
• The first World Championships were held in London in 1926.
 
• The Championships include events for both individual players and national teams.
 
• Over the years, the Championships have been held in various countries around the world, showcasing the global popularity of the sport.
 
 
 
• **International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF):**
 
 
• The ITTF is the governing body for all international table tennis associations.
 
• It was founded in 1926 and is responsible for the organization of numerous international competitions, including the World Table Tennis Championships.
 
• The ITTF oversees the rules and regulations of the sport, ensuring fair play and standardization across the globe.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Hosting International Events:**
 
 
• Hosting international sports events can significantly boost a country's visibility and reputation in the global arena.

questions.question: How many chambers are there in the heart of fishes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fishes have a **two-chambered heart** consisting of one atrium and one ventricle.
 
• The blood flows in a single circuit, from the heart to the gills for oxygenation and then to the rest of the body.
 
• The two-chambered heart is efficient for the aquatic life of fishes, supporting their metabolism and oxygen needs.
 
• Having a two-chambered heart is a characteristic feature of **most fish species**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chambers of the Heart**

 
 
• **Atrium:** The atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the body and sends it to the ventricle.
 
• **Ventricle:** The ventricle pumps the deoxygenated blood to the gills for oxygenation.
 
 
 
• **Circulatory System in Fishes**
 
 
• Fishes have a **single circulatory system**, meaning blood passes through the heart only once during each complete circuit of the body.
 
• After oxygenation in the gills, the oxygen-rich blood is delivered directly to the tissues without returning to the heart.
 
• This system is different from mammals and birds, which have a double circulatory system.
 
 
 
• **Gills**
 
 
• Gills are the respiratory organs in fishes that allow them to extract oxygen from water.
 
• Blood flows through the gill filaments where gas exchange occurs – carbon dioxide is released into the water and oxygen is absorbed.
 
 
 
• **Adaptations**
 
 
• The two-chambered heart and single circulatory system are highly adapted to an aquatic environment where oxygen levels can vary.
 
• These adaptations ensure efficient oxygen delivery to support the metabolism and activity levels of fishes.

questions.question: As per the report of the NITI Aayog in 2023, which among the following states in India has the lowest percentage of the total population that is multidimensionally poor?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the NITI Aayog report of 2023, Kerala has the lowest percentage of the total population that is multidimensionally poor.
 
• Kerala's robust health and education infrastructure contribute significantly to its low multidimensional poverty rate.
 
• The state has consistently performed well in various human development indices, including literacy and life expectancy.
 
• Kerala's social policies and investments in public services have played a crucial role in reducing poverty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**

 
 
• The MPI is a measure that captures the multiple deprivations that people face in their daily lives, including poor health, lack of education, and inadequate living standards.
 
• It is an international measure developed by the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• The MPI assesses poverty at the individual level by considering various factors like nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, school attendance, cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, and assets.
 
• The MPI helps policymakers target resources and interventions more effectively to address the specific needs of the poor.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog**
 
 
• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) is the premier policy think tank of the Government of India, providing both directional and policy inputs.
 
• It was established in 2015, replacing the Planning Commission of India, with the aim to foster cooperative federalism through structured support initiatives and mechanisms with the states on a continuous basis.
 
• NITI Aayog's primary objectives include promoting sustainable development, enhancing the use of technology, and improving governance and policy implementation.
 
• It plays a crucial role in designing strategic and long-term policies and programs for the Government of India.
 
 
 
• **Human Development Index (HDI)**
 
 
• The HDI is a composite statistic of life expectancy, education, and per capita income indicators, which are used to rank countries into four tiers of human development.
 
• It is a measure of a country's social and economic development, developed by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• HDI scores are used to assess and compare the level of human development across countries and regions.
 
• The HDI helps in understanding the broader picture of development and guiding policy decisions to improve living conditions.

questions.question: What is the unit of measurement for optical power of the lens?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diopter**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The diopter (D) is the unit of measurement for the optical power of a lens or curved mirror.
 
• It is defined as the reciprocal of the focal length (f) measured in meters (i.e., D = 1/f).
 
• A lens with a focal length of 1 meter has an optical power of 1 diopter.
 
• Lenses with positive diopters are converging lenses, while those with negative diopters are diverging lenses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Optical Power:**

 
 
• Optical power, also known as lens power, is the degree to which a lens converges or diverges light.
 
• It is an important concept in optics and is essential in the design of optical systems such as glasses, cameras, and telescopes.
 
 
 
• **Focal Length:**
 
 
• The focal length of a lens is the distance from the lens at which parallel rays of light converge to a single point.
 
• It determines the magnifying power of the lens and is crucial in the formation of clear images.
 
 
 
• **Converging and Diverging Lenses:**
 
 
• Converging lenses (positive diopters) focus light to a point and are used in applications like magnifying glasses and corrective lenses for hyperopia (farsightedness).
 
• Diverging lenses (negative diopters) spread light outwards and are used in devices like peepholes and corrective lenses for myopia (nearsightedness).

questions.question:
The Government of India allowed automatic approval of _____% of FDI by Reserve Bank of India in nine categories of

industries.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Up to 74%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India has allowed automatic approval of up to 74% Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) by the Reserve Bank of India in nine categories of industries.
 
• This move was aimed at simplifying the investment process and making it more attractive for foreign investors.
 
• FDI is a major source of non-debt financial resource for the economic development of India.
 
• Automatic approval means that foreign investors do not need prior approval from the government for investment up to 74% in these industries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI):**

 
 
• FDI refers to the investment made by a firm or individual in one country into business interests located in another country.
 
• It usually involves participation in management, joint-venture, transfer of technology and expertise.
 
• FDI is considered crucial for the economic development of a country as it brings in capital, technology, and expertise.
 
 
 
• **Automatic Route:**
 
 
• Under the automatic route, foreign investment does not require prior approval from the government or the Reserve Bank of India.
 
• Investors are only required to inform the Reserve Bank's regional office within 30 days of receipt of inward remittances and file the required documents.
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**
 
 
• The RBI is the central banking institution of India, which controls the issuance and supply of the Indian rupee and oversees the country's monetary policy.
 
• It also plays an essential role in regulating the financial system and ensuring its stability.
 
 
 
• **Industries Eligible for 74% FDI:**
 
 
• The government has specified nine categories of industries where up to 74% FDI is allowed under the automatic route.
 
• These categories include sectors like pharmaceuticals, telecommunications, and various manufacturing industries.

questions.question: Who among the following was the last sultan of Delhi sultanate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ibrahim Lodi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ibrahim Lodi** was the last ruler of the Delhi Sultanate from the Lodi dynasty.
 
• He reigned from 1517 until his defeat and death in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.
 
• Ibrahim Lodi was the son of Sikandar Lodi and ascended to the throne after his father's death.
 
• His rule marked the end of the Delhi Sultanate and the beginning of the Mughal Empire in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delhi Sultanate**

 
 
• The Delhi Sultanate was a Muslim kingdom that ruled over large parts of the Indian subcontinent for over 300 years, from 1206 to 1526.
 
• It was established by Qutb-ud-din Aibak after the defeat of Prithviraj Chauhan and marked the beginning of Muslim rule in India.
 
• The Sultanate saw the rise and fall of several dynasties including the Mamluks, Khaljis, Tughlaqs, Sayyids, and Lodis.
 
• It played a crucial role in shaping the culture, architecture, and administration of India during the medieval period.
 
 
 
• **First Battle of Panipat**
 
 
• The First Battle of Panipat was fought on April 21, 1526, between the forces of the Mughal ruler Babur and the Lodi dynasty's Sultan Ibrahim Lodi.
 
• The battle marked the end of the Delhi Sultanate and the beginning of the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• Babur's use of innovative military tactics and artillery was instrumental in his victory.
 
• This battle is considered one of the most significant events in Indian history as it led to the establishment of Mughal rule, which lasted for over three centuries.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Empire**
 
 
• The Mughal Empire was an empire that controlled large parts of the Indian subcontinent from the early 16th to the mid-19th century.
 
• It was founded by Babur, a descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan, after his victory in the First Battle of Panipat.
 
• The Mughal Empire is known for its rich cultural contributions, including significant developments in art, architecture, and cuisine.
 
• Some of the most famous Mughal rulers include Akbar, Shah Jahan, and Aurangzeb.

questions.question: In the context of water bodies, Neap Tides occur:

options.text: when the earth, moon and sun line up in a straight line
when the sun and moon are on the opposite sides
when there is so much interference by continents
when the sun and moon are at right angles to each other

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**when the sun and moon are at right angles to each other**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Neap tides occur when the gravitational forces of the moon and the sun are perpendicular to one another with respect to the Earth.
 
• These tides are characterized by the least difference between high and low tide levels, making them weaker compared to spring tides.
 
• Neap tides occur during the first and third quarters of the moon phase, approximately every two weeks.
 
• During neap tides, the tidal range is reduced because the sun's gravitational pull partially cancels out the moon's gravitational pull on the Earth's oceans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Spring Tides**

 
 
• Spring tides occur when the Earth, moon, and sun are aligned, leading to the highest high tides and the lowest low tides.
 
• This alignment occurs during full moon and new moon phases.
 
• The combined gravitational force of the moon and sun leads to a greater tidal range.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Forces**
 
 
• The gravitational forces of the moon and sun both affect the Earth's oceans, causing tides.
 
• The moon's gravitational force has a more significant impact due to its proximity to Earth.
 
 
 
• **Tidal Range**
 
 
• The tidal range is the difference in height between consecutive high and low tides.
 
• It varies depending on the alignment of the Earth, moon, and sun.
 
 
 
• **Phases of the Moon**
 
 
• The moon goes through different phases (new moon, first quarter, full moon, third quarter) as it orbits the Earth.
 
• These phases affect the gravitational pull on the Earth's oceans, leading to different types of tides.

questions.question: The idols of which three Gods are installed in Jagannath Temple, Puri?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Jagannath Temple in Puri is dedicated to Lord Jagannath (a form of Lord Vishnu).
 
• The temple also houses idols of Balabhadra (Lord Jagannath's elder brother) and Subhadra (their sister).
 
• This temple is one of the four Hindu pilgrimage sites known as the Char Dham.
 
• The idol of Jagannath is made of wood and is ceremoniously replaced every twelve or nineteen years in a process known as Nabakalebara.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jagannath Temple**

 
 
• Located in Puri, Odisha, the Jagannath Temple is a famous Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Jagannath.
 
• The temple is an important pilgrimage destination for Hindus, especially Vaishnavas.
 
• It is famous for its annual Ratha Yatra or Chariot Festival, where the three principal deities are pulled on huge and elaborately decorated temple cars.
 
• Non-Hindus are not allowed to enter the temple premises, but they can view the temple from the nearby Raghunandan Library.
 
 
 
• **Char Dham**
 
 
• Char Dham refers to the four holy pilgrimage sites for Hindus, which include Badrinath, Dwarka, Puri, and Rameswaram.
 
• These sites are highly revered and are visited by devotees to attain spiritual salvation.
 
• The pilgrimage to Char Dham is considered a way to cleanse oneself of sins and attain Moksha (liberation).
 
 
 
• **Nabakalebara**
 
 
• Nabakalebara is a ritual that involves the renewal of the wooden idols of Jagannath, Balabhadra, Subhadra, and Sudarshana.
 
• This ritual is performed when there are two Ashadha months in a year, which happens according to the Hindu calendar approximately every 12 to 19 years.
 
• During Nabakalebara, new idols are carved from specially chosen neem trees, and the old idols are buried in a sacred place within the temple premises.

questions.question: As in July 2021, The NIPUN Bharat Scheme was launched by which of the following Ministries?

options.text: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Education**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The NIPUN Bharat Scheme was launched by the Ministry of Education in July 2021.
 
• NIPUN stands for National Initiative for Proficiency in Reading with Understanding and Numeracy.
 
• The aim of the NIPUN Bharat Scheme is to ensure that every child in India attains foundational literacy and numeracy by the end of Grade 3, by 2026-27.
 
• The scheme is an essential part of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 which focuses on early education and foundational learning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**

 
 
• The NEP 2020 is a comprehensive framework to guide the development of education in the country.
 
 
• **Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN)**
 
 
• FLN refers to the basic reading, writing, and arithmetic skills that form the foundation of a child's education.
 
• The NIPUN Bharat scheme specifically targets the attainment of FLN by children at the primary level.
 
• FLN is crucial for the overall cognitive development of a child and impacts their ability to learn more complex subjects in higher grades.
 
 
 
• **Implementation of NIPUN Bharat**
 
 
• The scheme is implemented by the Department of School Education and Literacy under the Ministry of Education.
 
• It involves the training of teachers, the development of age-appropriate learning materials, and regular assessments to track progress.
 
• The initiative promotes a participatory approach involving parents, community members, and local bodies to ensure the effective implementation of the scheme.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India expressly provides that the President is eligible for re-election?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 57**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 57 of the Constitution of India states that a person who holds, or who has held, office as President shall, subject to the other provisions of this Constitution, be eligible for re-election to that office.
 
• This article ensures that there is no restriction on the number of times a person can be re-elected as President of India.
 
• The President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States.
 
• Article 57 is part of the chapter on the Executive, which is detailed in Part V of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 56**

 
 
• Article 56 of the Constitution of India deals with the term of office of the President.
 
• According to this article, the President shall hold office for a term of five years from the date on which he enters upon his office.
 
• The President may resign from his office by writing under his hand addressed to the Vice-President of India.
 
• The President may, for violation of the Constitution, be removed from office by impeachment in the manner provided in Article 61.
 
 
 
• **Article 58**
 
 
• Article 58 lays down the qualifications for election as President of India.
 
• A person shall be eligible for election as President if he is a citizen of India, has completed the age of thirty-five years, and is qualified for election as a member of the House of the People.
 
• The person should not hold any office of profit under the Government of India or the Government of any State or under any local or other authority subject to the control of any of the said Governments.
 
 
 
• **Article 59**
 
 
• Article 59 deals with the conditions of the President's office.
 
• The President shall not be a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any State, and if a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the Legislature of any State be elected President, he shall be deemed to have vacated his seat in that House on the date on which he enters upon his office as President.
 
• The President shall not hold any other office of profit.
 
• The President shall be entitled to such emoluments, allowances, and privileges as may be determined by Parliament by law and, until provision in that behalf is so made, such emoluments, allowances, and privileges as are specified in the Second Schedule.
 
• The emoluments and allowances of the President shall not be diminished during his term of office.

questions.question: In which of the following cities did Mahatma Gandhi lead the peasant movement against the imposed indigo cultivation by the British planters?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Champaran**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Champaran is famous for the Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 where Mahatma Gandhi led a movement against the British planters who forced local farmers to grow indigo under harsh conditions.
 
• This movement marked Gandhi's first active involvement in the Indian freedom struggle and was a significant milestone in India's path to independence.
 
• The success of the Champaran movement brought Gandhi to the forefront of the Indian independence movement.
 
• The indigo planters in Champaran were exploiting the farmers by forcing them to grow indigo on a portion of their land and sell it at fixed prices, which was economically detrimental to the farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**

 
 
• Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, popularly known as Mahatma Gandhi, was a prominent leader of the Indian independence movement against British rule.
 
• He is known for his philosophy of non-violence (Ahimsa) and civil disobedience, which he employed to lead India to independence.
 
• Gandhi's methods inspired movements for civil rights and freedom across the world.
 
• He is often referred to as the "Father of the Nation" in India for his pivotal role in the country's struggle for independence.
 
 
 
• **Indigo Cultivation**
 
 
• Indigo was a valuable dye in the textile industry during the colonial period.
 
• British planters in India forced local farmers to grow indigo under the Tinkathia system, where farmers had to grow indigo on 3/20th (or roughly 15%) of their land.
 
• This system was highly exploitative as the indigo crop depleted the soil, and the farmers received very low prices for their produce.
 
• The Champaran Satyagraha was a protest against this system and highlighted the plight of the farmers.
 
 
 
• **Satyagraha**
 
 
• Satyagraha is a form of nonviolent resistance or civil resistance.
 
• The term was coined and developed by Mahatma Gandhi during the Indian independence movement.
 
• Satyagraha is based on the principle of nonviolence and seeks to bring about social and political change through passive resistance and peaceful protests.
 
• It emphasizes the power of truth and the need to adhere to ethical principles in the face of injustice.

questions.question: According to the Ashrama system of Vedic life, which of the following was the third stage of life?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Vanaprastha is the third stage in the Ashrama system of Vedic life, typically starting around the age of 50 when a person withdraws from worldly responsibilities.
 
• This stage is characterized by retirement from household duties and the beginning of a spiritual journey.
 
• Individuals in the Vanaprastha stage often spend their time in forests or secluded places for meditation and spiritual practices.
 
• The Vanaprastha stage serves as a transition from the Grihastha (householder) stage to Sanyasa (renunciation), emphasizing detachment from material possessions and societal roles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmacharya**

 
 
• This is the first stage of life in the Ashrama system, focusing on education and celibacy.
 
• It typically lasts until the age of 25, during which an individual is expected to live a disciplined life of study and self-control.
 
 
 
• **Grihastha**
 
 
• The second stage of life, starting around the age of 25 and lasting until about 50.
 
• It involves marriage, family responsibilities, and contributing to society through work and raising children.
 
 
 
• **Sanyasa**
 
 
• The fourth and final stage of life, marked by renunciation of worldly possessions and responsibilities.
 
• Individuals in this
 
• 
 
 
• Individuals in this stage dedicate their lives to spiritual pursuits and often become wandering ascetics.

• **Ashrama System**
 
 
• The Ashrama system is a framework for the stages of life in Hindu philosophy, guiding an individual's journey from birth to death.
 
• The four stages are Brahmacharya (student life), Grihastha (householder life), Vanaprastha (hermit or forest-dweller life), and Sanyasa (renounced life).
